security_audit.summary: The review confirms real boundary risks from sibling-package references and hidden home-directory workflow loading. Most other alerts are false positives from Markdown code spans, official user-facing URLs, and protective credential warnings. No prompt-injection text was found in the reviewed files, but the shared preflight also adds installer and update risk.

remediation.issue: Cross-package references escape the reviewed skill directory.
remediation.suggestion: Bundle required guidance in this package or use a pinned marketplace dependency with its own completed audit.

remediation.issue: Workflow routing loads hidden files from the user home directory.
remediation.suggestion: Use packaged workflow files, or require explicit user confirmation and an allowlist of exact workflow filenames.

remediation.issue: The shared preflight can install or update local tooling.
remediation.suggestion: Remove automatic install and forced update steps. Ask the user to approve manual install steps with checksum verification.

finding_verdicts.reason: The line tells users to add any .env file to .gitignore when using a personal key. It does not read, create, or expose an environment file.
The skill directs the agent to read ../../okx-agentic-wallet/SKILL.md, which escapes the skill package boundary. Loading sibling skill content can import unreviewed instructions.
The URL is a user-facing Help Center link in a guidance-only response. The file explicitly says it makes no CLI call, network request, wallet access, or side effect.
The URL is part of manual support instructions for the user to click. It does not cause automated network access or data transfer by the agent.
The backticks mark the literal environment variable name OKX_API_KEY in Markdown. There is no Ruby or shell backtick execution on this line.
The backticks mark the literal environment variable name OKX_SECRET_KEY in Markdown. There is no command substitution or executable shell syntax.
The backticks mark the literal environment variable name OKX_PASSPHRASE in Markdown. The surrounding text is credential guidance, not shell execution.
The hardcoded URL points users to the OKX developer portal to obtain credentials. It is a manual documentation link and not an automated outbound request.
The flow auto-loads ~/.onchainos/workflows/daily-brief.md after login. Reading executable prompt content from a hidden home directory is a real boundary and prompt-injection risk.
The flow auto-loads ~/.onchainos/workflows/<file>.md based on a workflow pick. The dynamic hidden-home path can import local prompt content outside the reviewed package.
The same line instructs the agent to load a hidden-home workflow file. That is legitimate product behavior, but it still reads unreviewed local prompt content.
The same line instructs the agent to load a hidden-home workflow file selected from a route. The reviewed skill does not contain or validate the target file.
The line lists the name of a required OKX API key variable for local setup. The file later forbids pasting credentials into chat and does not read the value.
The line lists the name of a required OKX secret key variable for local setup. The surrounding flow tells users to set secrets locally and not disclose them.
The line is a prohibition against creating .env files or editing .gitignore during the flow. It reduces credential-handling risk rather than accessing files.
The line routes named DApp requests to an existing discovery skill. It does not enumerate the host system or collect local environment details.
The status mapping relies on ../../okx-ai/references/identity-invariants.md outside this skill. Cross-package reads can import instructions that were not reviewed with this package.
The registration path loads ../../okx-ai/references/identity-register.md outside the skill boundary. That delegates control to external prompt content from a sibling package.
The command queries current tasks for user-supplied Agent IDs as part of the product workflow. The text constrains the request and handles unauthorized IDs instead of probing networks.
Selecting the User role loads ../../okx-ai/references/identity-register.md outside this package. That is a real package-boundary escape even if the target is intentional.
Selecting the ASP role loads the same ../../okx-ai registration playbook outside this package. The skill depends on unbundled sibling instructions.
Selecting the Evaluator role loads the same ../../okx-ai registration playbook outside this package. This crosses the reviewed skill boundary for a privileged registration flow.
The menu routes a logged-in daily brief pick to ~/.onchainos/workflows/daily-brief.md. Loading hidden-home prompt files is outside the audited skill content.
The alternate menu variant also routes daily brief to ~/.onchainos/workflows/daily-brief.md. The target file is local hidden-home content and is not packaged here.
The logged-in branch directly loads ~/.onchainos/workflows/daily-brief.md. That creates a real hidden-home file access and prompt-import risk.
The line instructs loading the hidden daily-brief workflow from the user home directory. This is intentional behavior but still imports unreviewed local content.
The line repeats the hidden daily-brief workflow load for another menu variant. It is a real hidden file read outside the marketplace-reviewed package.
The logged-in branch explicitly loads a hidden workflow file from ~/.onchainos. That file is not included in this skill audit.
The line describes handling an expired wallet session when wallet balance fails. It does not collect system inventory or perform host reconnaissance.
The flagged backticks are Markdown around reference paths, not shell command substitution. The preflight delegation has separate risk, but this static pattern is not Ruby or shell execution.
The line uses Markdown code spans for a file name and a read-only CLI command name. It does not use Ruby backticks or shell command substitution.
The line states that support is conversation-only with no CLI. The backticks are only Markdown around a file name.
The line is an intent-routing table with a Markdown link to a local reference file. It contains no executable shell or Ruby syntax.
The line is an intent-routing table with a Markdown link to ai-guide.md. It is not command execution.
The line is an intent-routing table with a Markdown link to ai-support.md. The detected backticks are not shell execution.
The URL is homepage metadata for OKX Web3. It does not instruct the agent to make a network request or transmit user data.

semantic_findings.title: Automatic Installer and Update Flow
semantic_findings.description: The shared preflight can update binaries and skill checkouts, run a forced upgrade command, and download installation scripts when the CLI is missing. A community skill should not trigger tool installation or updates without explicit marketplace-controlled confirmation.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The file directly instructs running preflight and fallback installer behavior, including upgrade and install script steps. The risk is contextual because it depends on external onchainos tooling, but the intent is clear.

content.user_title: Navigate Onchain OS and OKX.AI Onboarding
content.value_statement: New users need help choosing the right Onchain OS path without exposing wallet secrets. This skill routes onboarding, OKX.AI, and support requests through guided flows.
actual_capabilities: Classifies requests as Onchain OS onboarding, OKX.AI guidance, or customer support.
Shows logged-in or logged-out welcome menus based on wallet status.
Guides users through email or API key login choices without collecting secrets.
Detects whether the current AI runtime can support OKX.AI flows.
Routes OKX.AI users to role selection, registered-user home, or support guidance.
Localizes menu text while preserving IDs, addresses, URLs, and placeholders.
limitations: It does not perform swaps, balance transfers, or direct token actions.
It delegates OKX.AI registration and wallet login to other skills or flows.
Some workflows require the onchainos CLI and a compatible agent runtime.
It cannot accept API keys, passphrases, or wallet secrets in chat.

use_cases.title: Start With Onchain OS
use_cases.description: A new wallet user gets a clear menu for OKX.AI, DeFi yield, Polymarket, or daily market briefs.

use_cases.title: Choose an OKX.AI Role
use_cases.description: An agent economy participant learns whether to register as a User, ASP, or Evaluator.

use_cases.title: Find Support Fast
use_cases.description: A user with a complaint or bug report receives the OKX.AI Help Center steps.

prompt_templates.title: Get Started
prompt_templates.prompt: I am new to Onchain OS. Show me where to start.

prompt_templates.title: Understand OKX.AI
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain what OKX.AI is and help me choose the right role.

prompt_templates.title: Resume After Login
prompt_templates.prompt: I picked the daily brief before logging in. Continue from that choice after login.

prompt_templates.title: Review Agent Tasks
prompt_templates.prompt: I already have an OKX.AI identity. Show my home view and help me check an Agent task.

output_examples.input: What can I do with Onchain OS?
output_examples.output: A localized welcome menu with an OKX.AI highlight, available workflow options, and a trading caution disclaimer.
A role selection flow that explains User, ASP, and Evaluator paths, then waits for a role choice.
A short Help Center walkthrough that explains how to open support chat on the OKX.AI website.

best_practices: Use it for onboarding, OKX.AI role guidance, or support routing requests.
Complete wallet login locally and never paste credentials into the conversation.
Follow the displayed menu numbers because choices can change by region and login state.
anti_patterns: Do not use it for swaps, token transfers, or direct on-chain trade execution.
Do not paste API keys, secret keys, passphrases, or wallet recovery data.
Do not ask it to bypass geoblocked or unavailable menu options.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It guides users through Onchain OS onboarding, OKX.AI role paths, wallet login choices, and support routing.

faq.question: Does it make on-chain transactions?
faq.answer: No. It routes and explains flows. Other skills handle transaction-specific actions when appropriate.

faq.question: Can I paste API keys into chat?
faq.answer: No. Set credentials locally and rotate any secret that was pasted into a conversation.

faq.question: Does it support Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists compatibility with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Why do menu numbers change?
faq.answer: The visible options depend on login state and availability checks. Reply using the menu currently shown.

faq.question: Can it help me contact OKX.AI support?
faq.answer: Yes. It provides the Help Center link and steps to start support chat.
